title: From Elementary to Perfection
english: Let us be brought to the state of 'we carry the nature'. Let us leave the elementary word, for it is the beginning of the teaching of Christ. Let us be led forward to perfection, so that having become perfect in this way, we may be able to be perfect hearers of Christ; for 'we speak wisdom among the perfect' (1 Cor 2:6).

Sometimes the soul is called, as I have already said, a sheep. When it is a sheep, it grazes on pasture, not on flesh, not on the flesh of Jesus, nor on bread. It is not yet able to have desire for these foods or to manage them, even if they are presented to it. It grazes on herbs; and herbs are spiritual. Sometimes it is also called a plant and needs rain; it grazes on the art of agriculture, so that having grown, it may bring forth perfect fruit somehow; 'but I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God'. And here, therefore, the sheep-like state, which is as it were more irrational, along with gentleness and stability, signifies through the saying: 'The Lord is my shepherd, and I shall not want' (Ps 23:1). I am without wandering, and without wandering as a sheep. Just as even a baby says: 'The nurse feeds me, and I shall not want', making it clear that it is of infantile foods.

The interpreter says: 'Into a place of pasture, there He pitched His tent'. There is a pasture-like teaching suitable to sheep. And perhaps this is no other than this voice of Christ; for He says: 'My sheep hear my voice' (John 10:27). The disciples of Christ, having become perfect according to His training, being no longer sheep, do not hear a voice, but they use Him as Teacher; for 'you' 'call Me' the Lord and the Teacher, and you say well: 'I am'. Therefore, 'into a place' 'of pasture, there He pitched His tent'. Not 'He dwelt', but 'He pitched His tent'. And the tent signifies progress; 'I shall pass through to a place of a wonderful tent until the house of God'. The one making progress has a portable dwelling, which is virtue itself. But when he reaches the goal and the end of it, he no longer pitches a tent, but dwells. This one, the holy man, knowing the greatness and the progress...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
